proof_summary: For even \(m\ge 8\), set \(n=m-1\); since \(n\) is odd, a witness prime \(p\) makes \(n-(p-1)=m-p\) prime, yielding \(m=p+(m-p)\). For odd \(m\ge 9\), set \(n=m-1\); since \(n\) is even, a witness prime \(q\) makes \(n-(2q-1)=m-2q\) prime, yielding \(m=(m-2q)+2q\), while \(4,6,7\) are handled by explicit prime decompositions.
